t.3.5.1: When Śarabhaṅga had attained heaven, the hosts of sages, having assembled together, approached Rāma the Kākutstha, whose splendour blazed brightly.
t.3.5.2: Many ascetics were there: Vaikhānasas, Vālakhilyas, Samprakṣālas and Marīcipas, Aśmakuṭṭas too, and ascetics who lived on leaves.
t.3.5.3: There were also sages who used their teeth as a mortar, and likewise others who kept themselves immersed in water; some munis lived on water alone, and others likewise lived on air.
t.3.5.5: And ascetics devoted to the muttering of prayers, constant in austerity, and likewise those who practiced the five-fire penance, all endowed with Brahmanic splendor and absorbed in steadfast yoga, approached Rāma at the hermitage of Śarabhaṅga.
t.3.5.4: There were ascetics who dwelt under the open sky, and likewise those who slept on the bare ground, those who lived on high places, the self-restrained, and those who wore wet garments.
t.3.5.6: And having approached Rāma, the best of those who uphold dharma and supreme knower of dharma, the hosts of sages, themselves knowers of dharma and with composed minds, spoke to him.
t.3.5.7: You, a great chariot-warrior, are the foremost and the lord of this Ikṣvāku dynasty and of the earth, just as Maghavān is of the gods.
t.3.5.8: You are renowned throughout the three worlds for your glory and your valour; in you dwell devotion to your father's vow, truthfulness, and abundant righteousness.
t.3.5.9: Having approached you, the great-souled one, knower of dharma and devoted to dharma, we shall speak, O lord, out of our need as supplicants; and you should forgive us for that.
t.3.5.10: But great unrighteousness, dear one, would befall that lord of the earth who takes a sixth part as tax and yet does not protect his subjects as his own sons.
t.3.5.12: O Rāma, he attains everlasting fame lasting for many years, and having reached the abode of Brahman, he is honored there as well.
t.3.5.13: Whatever supreme dharma a sage who lives on roots and fruits performs, a fourth part of it belongs to the king who protects his subjects in accordance with dharma.
t.3.5.11: Tending to all who dwell in his realm as though they were his own life-breaths, as though they were sons dear as life itself, ever devoted, he always protects them.
t.3.5.14: O Rāma, this great company of forest-dwelling hermits, made up mostly of brāhmaṇas, though it has you as its protector, is being cruelly slaughtered by the rākṣasas as though it had no protector at all.
t.3.5.15: Come, see the bodies of the many sages of perfected selves, slain in many ways by the dreadful rākṣasas here in the forest.
t.3.5.16: Great slaughter is being wrought upon those who dwell by the river Pampā, upon those along the Mandākinī, and upon those whose abode is Citrakūṭa.
t.3.5.17: Thus we cannot endure the terrible outrage being inflicted upon the ascetics in the forest by the Rākṣasas of fearsome deeds.
t.3.5.18: Therefore we have come to you, the giver of refuge, seeking refuge. O Rāma, protect us, who are being slain by the night-roaming demons.
t.3.5.19: Having heard this from the ascetics devoted to austerity, Kākutstha, whose soul was righteous, spoke these words to all the ascetics: "You ought not to speak to me thus; I am one to be commanded by the ascetics."
t.3.5.20: I have come here by chance, for the accomplishment of your purpose; this dwelling of mine in the forest will bear great fruit. I wish to slay in battle the rākṣasas, the enemies of the ascetics.
t.3.5.21: Having granted a boon to the ascetics, the hero, his mind steadfast in dharma and his conduct worthy of honour even among the ascetics, went together with Lakṣmaṇa straight to Sutīkṣṇa.
